subject: pe
title: Foundations of Sport Psychology
welcome_lead: Get inside the athlete's head — meet the mental forces that drive sport.
meta_desc: GCSE PE Sport Psychology foundations: arousal, motivation, goal setting, aggression.
final_note: Great work! You have unlocked the mental side of performance.

concepts.def: Physical and mental readiness to perform.
Drive from inside — enjoyment, pride, mastery.
Drive from outside — trophies, money, praise.
Physical contact intended to harm an opponent.
Aggression taken out on an object, not the opponent.
Forceful, fair play within the rules.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Inverted U Hypothesis says performance rises with arousal up to an optimal level, then falls if arousal becomes too high. Fine skills (archery) need lower arousal; gross skills (rugby) tolerate higher arousal.

Intrinsic — internal: love of the game, satisfaction, achievement. Extrinsic — external: trophies, prize money, recognition. Intrinsic motivation tends to be longer-lasting; extrinsic rewards can boost short-term effort.

Direct aggression is illegal contact aimed to hurt (a rugby high-tackle). Indirect aggression attacks an object instead (smashing a racket). Assertion is hard, fair, rule-following play. Only assertion is acceptable in sport.

mcqs.q: According to the Inverted U Hypothesis, performance is best at what level of arousal?
Winning a medal is an example of which type of motivation?

numericals.q: How many letters are in the SMART goal-setting acronym?

free_texts.q: Forceful but fair play within the rules of a sport is called what?
